breakNow: Time for a study break! Stand up, stretch, drink some water. 💧
title: Wellbeing
subtitle: Big goals need rest too. Check your balance and take care of yourself.
balanceHelp: How your scheduled week splits up. Sleep isn't counted — try for 8–10 hours a night.
balanceEmpty: Add your week in the Weekly schedule to see your balance.
ok: Your week looks balanced. Nice job protecting your rest! 🌿
busy: Your week is busy. That's okay sometimes — keep an eye on how you feel.
overloaded: Your week looks really full. It might be time to ease up a little. 💛
reason_heavy_days: You have {n} days with 11+ hours of school, practice, work or study.
reason_little_rest: There's very little rest or fun time scheduled.
reason_lots_of_work: You're working more than 20 hours a week during school.
reason_many_deadlines: You have several deadlines this week.
reason_too_many_hours: You've scheduled over 60 hours of commitments.
suggest1: Could you drop, move, or shorten one thing this week?
suggest2: Put a rest block on your schedule like any other appointment.
suggest3: Talk to a parent, coach, or counselor — they can help you prioritize.
checkin: How are you feeling this week?
reply_great: Love that! Keep doing what's working — and celebrate it.
reply_ok: Okay is okay. Try one small thing today that you enjoy.
reply_stressed: Stress happens to everyone. Try the breathing exercise below and pick ONE task to do first.
reply_bad: I'm sorry you're feeling this way. You don't have to handle it alone — please talk to a trusted adult or your counselor. If you ever feel unsafe, call or text 988.
breatheHelp: Box breathing: breathe in for 4, hold for 4, out for 4, hold for 4.
breaksHelp: Get a gentle reminder to take a break while Rumbo is open.
helpSub: Your counselor and free, private help lines
privacy: Your check-in answer isn't saved anywhere.
tip1: Do the hardest task first, when your energy is highest.
tip2: Put your phone in another room for 25 minutes of focused study.
tip3: A 10-minute walk outside can lower stress and help you focus.
tip4: Sleep is a superpower: teens need 8–10 hours to learn and remember.
tip5: Write down everything on your mind, then pick just one next step.
tip6: Drink water and eat something — it's hard to focus when you're hungry.
tip7: It's okay to say no to something to protect your time.
tip8: Text a friend or spend time with family — connection helps.
tip9: Break big projects into tiny steps you can finish in 15 minutes.
tip10: Do something just for fun this week, with no goal attached.
warnLink: Your schedule looks overloaded — see tips
